topic.title: The gym is built for people who won't come
topic.claim: Gyms push the annual plan hard because their business works best if most of the members who paid never show up.
topic.moment: The trainer says 'one year is basically half price' and you sign up on January 3rd feeling like a new person.

turn.believed: The yearly plan is a discount for committed people.
turn.actually: It's money paid upfront by people the gym expects to stop coming.

topic.feeling: Guilty every time I pass the gym, and they're happy I feel that way.
topic.villain: Upfront annual memberships sold on future motivation.
topic.because: A gym can only fit so many people. It sells far more memberships than it has space for, betting that most won't come.
topic.payoff: Pay monthly for three months. If you still go, the annual plan is a discount. If not, you just saved nine months.
topic.behaviour: Gyms offer steep annual discounts and push hardest in January and after Diwali.
topic.mechanism: Upfront money from members who drop off pays for the few who stay.
topic.group: Young working people trying to get fit
topic.send_to: The friend who has paid for a gym membership for the last three years in a row.
topic.why_now: Wellness spending is up, and annual plans are being pushed harder than ever.

score.why: The annual gym plan is money from people the gym expects to stop coming. The trap is the guilt you feel at the gate.
